source.title: ICLR Reproducibility Challenge Report (Padam : Closing The Generalization Gap Of Adaptive Gradient Methods in Training Deep Neural Networks)
source.authors: Harshal Mittal; Kartikey Pandey; Yash Kant

record.tranche_reason: Compares test performance of adaptive optimizers, SGD with momentum, and Padam on image classifiers using a reproduction setup rather than the original optimizer-comparison studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparison outcomes relevant to V4. It does not test the other claim versions. Figure-only comparisons are included only where the text describes their result; exact values are not reconstructed from plots.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out image-classification performance after training with Adam, Amsgrad and momentum SGD, using the same basic experimental method and measure as V4's optimizer comparisons. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Padam combines benefits of adaptive methods and momentum SGD, reporting comparable CIFAR-10 test error and intermediate convergence speed. They also emphasize that p requires tuning and depends on learning rate. Scheduling p and combining Padam with decoupled weight decay are proposed future experiments, not demonstrated improvements.
record.recipe_differences: Reproduction of Padam comparisons on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using VGGNet, ResNet, and Wide ResNet; ImageNet experiments were omitted. Optimizer hyperparameters and implementation details differ or are incompletely disclosed relative to the original work.
record.method_sensitivity: The report finds that the best partially adaptive parameter p depends on the base learning rate; higher p performed better with lower learning rates, while smaller p favored higher learning rates.
record.problems: The authors could not run ImageNet experiments because of time and computing-resource constraints. AdamW was not evaluated because its experiment details were not completely disclosed. Several optimizer comparisons are shown only in plots, with no exact values stated in the text; no uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, word-level language models, broader tuning of Adam versus SGD, AdamW, and switching from Adam to SGD. Equal or better final training performance cannot be established from the supplied plot text. The baseline comparison uses prescribed settings with different weight-decay coefficients, rather than establishing an optimizer difference under a common learning-rate-only tuning protocol.
Batch-size effects and adaptations to large-batch training.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Earlier checkpoint comparisons reverse the final Adam/Amsgrad ranking. CIFAR-10 at epochs 50/100: SGD 68.71/87.88%, Adam 84.62/91.54%, Amsgrad 87.89/91.75%. CIFAR-100: SGD 37.29/61.18%, Adam 55.44/65.67%, Amsgrad 58.85/68.21%.

Padam's held-out performance depends jointly on p and learning rate. ResNet experiments find p=0.125 best among three tested values at the specified schedule, while lower learning rates favor larger p and higher learning rates favor smaller p. These qualify the Padam parity result; exact plot values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Only V4 is tested. Different prescribed weight decay for SGD/Padam and Adam/Amsgrad limits causal attribution to optimizer choice alone. No uncertainty estimates establish whether the small CIFAR-10 differences or Padam advantages are reliable. The supplied text contains plot labels but no readable curves, so additional architecture-specific numerical rankings cannot be recovered.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Language benchmarks; broader optimizer tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
